submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 2.5 cm provides the best achievable pion/kaon separation (3.909 sigma) while meeting the critical humidity aging constraint. While Radiator-R2 offers superior separation performance (4.662 sigma at 4 cm), its porous structure without hydrophobic treatment makes it unsuitable for the mandatory 10-year humidity aging requirement. R3's hydrophobic treatment was specifically developed to enable porous radiators to withstand humidity exposure, making it the only high-performance option that can meet the aging constraint. R1, though stable, provides significantly worse separation (2.924 sigma). The 2.5 cm thickness optimizes R3's performance within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 2.5 cm achieves 3.909 sigma separation, which is the best performance among radiators that can meet the aging constraint. While R2 offers higher separation (4.662 sigma), it likely fails the aging requirement.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as 'porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment'.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R3's hydrophobic treatment was specifically designed to address humidity degradation in porous radiators. The existence of this treated variant (R3) versus untreated porous radiator (R2) indicates R3 meets the aging requirement while R2 does not.
The recommended thickness of 2.5 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.
